site.name: Pardesiya
site.tagline: Travel with the grain of the country — not against it.
site.intro: Pardesiya is a host for slow travel across India: a planner, a gallery, and a circle of people who still believe a journey should leave you more literate in someone else’s street. We map festivals, food, language, art, and the rooms that never make the brochure.

sidePanel.title: How to arrive
sidePanel.body: Land with curiosity. Learn one greeting, one sweet, one neighbourhood walk before the monument.

sidePanel.title: Monsoon window
sidePanel.body: Western ghats and Kerala glow after first rains. Forts of Maharashtra are a green theatre.

sidePanel.title: Craft, not costume
sidePanel.body: Buy from the workshop. Ask who dyed the cloth. Carry less plastic than you think you need.

sidePanel.title: Forum is open
sidePanel.body: Travellers and hosts will soon swap routes, warnings, and invitations. The square is being swept.

site.vision: We want a India that is visited without being flattened. Pardesiya exists so culture can be met in its own tempo — state by state, table by table — and so a small brand can send a little money back to makers. Know us more: we are hosts, not influencers with a drone.

brand.title: Brand story
brand.body: Pardesiya began as a collaboration: one of us walking with a notebook through family towns, the other photographing doorframes and thalis. We were tired of itineraries that treated India as a checklist. This house is built from those walks — a planner, a shop of makers, and a gallery that prefers people to monuments. The photograph on this wall is from an early trip; the story is still being written with everyone who hosts us.

states.name: Goa
states.tagline: Konkan churches, spice, and slow tide

categories.culture: Goa is not only a beach. Konkani life, Catholic feasts, and Hindu village temples share a small coastal state with a long Portuguese chapter.
categories.festival: Carnival, Sao Joao, and Shigmo. Feasts are neighbourhood events, not shows.
categories.language: Konkani, with Marathi, English, and traces of Portuguese in kitchens and churches.
categories.art: Azulejo-influenced tiles, church music, and contemporary art in Fontainhas.
categories.food: Prawn balchão, bebinca, xacuti, and feni. Vinegar and coconut argue productively.
categories.hiddenGems: Divar ferries, spice estates inland, and village tavernas far from the night market.

categories.culture: Gujarat’s mercantile confidence shows in pols, stepwells, and a craft map that still employs whole talukas.
categories.festival: Navratri’s garba, Rann Utsav, and Uttarayan when the sky fills with kites.
categories.language: Gujarati, with Kachchhi and a trading English that is older than the airports.
categories.art: Ajrakh, bandhani, embroidery of Kutch, and the wooden haveli.
categories.food: A thali that argues sweet and salty at once; fafda, undhiyu, and Gujarati kadhi.
categories.hiddenGems: Modhera’s sun temple at late light, the salt desert at night, and village block-printers in Dhamadka.

categories.culture: Himachal’s village gods travel in palanquins. Hill stations are a colonial layer over much older pahari worlds.
categories.festival: Kullu Dussehra, Losar in Buddhist valleys, and local fairs where deities meet.
categories.language: Pahari varieties and Hindi, with Tibetan in exile communities of Dharamshala.
categories.art: Pahari miniature painting, wood-carved temples, and thangka in the rain-shadow valleys.
categories.food: Siddu, dham thalis, trout, and apple everything in season.
categories.hiddenGems: Tirthan valley, the mud villages of Spiti, and deodar shrines that never needed a hashtag.

states.name: Karnataka
states.tagline: Stone empires and a coffee shade

categories.culture: Karnataka holds Vijayanagara’s ruins, a classical music school, and a tech city that still eats ragi.
categories.festival: Mysuru Dasara, Ugadi, and temple rathas in the old towns.
categories.language: Kannada, with Tulu and Kodava in the south and west.
categories.art: Hoysala stone, Mysore painting, and Yakshagana’s night-long theatre.
categories.food: Bisi bele bath, Neer dosa, Coorg pork, and filter coffee as ritual.
categories.hiddenGems: Lesser Hoysala shrines around Halebidu, the islands of the Tungabhadra, and coffee estate roads after rain.

categories.culture: Kerala’s public life mixes temple arts, Christian and Muslim coastal towns, and a strong reading culture. The houseboat and the courtyard house are both ways of living with water.
categories.festival: Onam’s pookalam and sadya, Thrissur Pooram’s elephants, and Theyyam in the north — seasons are marked by ritual theatre.
categories.language: Malayalam, with a literary tradition that travels easily into cinema and poetry.
categories.art: Kathakali, Mohiniyattam, mural painting, and coir and bronze craft. Faces become stories in makeup and lamp-light.
categories.food: Sadya on banana leaf, appam with stew, Malabar biryani, and toddy-shop karimeen. Coconut, curry leaf, and tamarind do the quiet work.
categories.hiddenGems: Wayanad’s groves, the Jewish traces of Mattancherry beyond the postcard, and village theyyam nights in Kannur.

states.name: Punjab
states.tagline: Langar, fields, and a loud heart

categories.culture: Punjab’s culture is hospitality at scale — langar, harvest, and music that does not whisper. The Golden Temple is both shrine and civic square.
categories.festival: Baisakhi, Lohri, and Maghi. Winter bonfires and spring harvest share the same drum.
categories.language: Punjabi, written in Gurmukhi, sung in every register from hymn to bhangra.
categories.art: Phulkari embroidery, metalwork, and a popular music industry that travels the world.
categories.food: Makki di roti, sarson da saag, Amritsari kulcha, lassi as thick as a story.
categories.hiddenGems: Border villages near Hussainiwala, Qila Mubarak’s rooms in Patiala, and roadside dhabas that outcook the city.

categories.culture: Rajasthan’s courtly manners, folk ballads, and desert hospitality still shape how guests are received. Palaces, havelis, and village courtyards keep a public culture of colour, honour, and music.
categories.festival: Teej, Gangaur, and the Desert Festival in Jaisalmer fill streets with processions, camels, and ghoomar. Diwali here is a city of lamps on sandstone.
categories.language: Rajasthani languages — Marwari, Mewari, Dhundhari and others — sit beside Hindi. Folk epics like Pabuji ki Phad are still sung, not only archived.
categories.art: Blue pottery, miniature painting, block-printed textiles, and the Phad scrolls of Bhilwara. Walls and fabrics are canvases.
categories.food: Dal baati churma, laal maas, ker sangri, and ghewar. Spice is slow-cooked, not rushed; sweets arrive like jewellery.
categories.hiddenGems: Bundi’s painted palaces, Shekhawati’s open-air fresco towns, and the salt flats around Sambhar reward travellers who leave the Golden Triangle loop.

categories.festival: Pongal, Chennai’s music season, and chariot festivals that turn streets into processional architecture.
categories.language: Tamil — classical and contemporary, from Sangam verse to cinema dialogue.
categories.art: Bharatanatyam, bronze casting of Swamimalai, Tanjore painting, and Kolam drawn at dawn.
categories.food: Idli, dosa, Chettinad pepper heat, filter coffee, and temple prasadam that is also a cuisine.
categories.hiddenGems: Chettinad mansions, the quiet tanks of smaller Chola shrines, and the salt air of fishing hamlets south of Chennai.

categories.language: Bangla — poetry, protest, and film in the same breath.
